metadata.note: The Wolfeboro Railroad was a 12-mile branch from Sanbornville (on the Portsmouth, Great Falls and Conway Railroad, see pgfc_railroad.geojson) to Wolfeboro on Lake Winnipesaukee, built specifically to carry lake-resort tourist traffic. The Wolfeborough Railroad Company was founded July 1 1868; construction began November 1871 and the line opened for traffic August 19 1872, operated by the Eastern Railroad. The Boston and Maine purchased it in 1892 and ran it until 1936. A private group revived it as a tourist excursion operation from 1972-1986 (not scheduled passenger service; not modeled as a separate segment here). Geometry re-traced from OpenStreetMap on 2026-08-24. The previous version was routed by Dijkstra between geocoded Sanbornville and Wolfeboro points and went the wrong way out of Sanbornville -- north up the ex-Boston & Maine Conway Branch (today's New Hampshire Northcoast Railroad) toward Ossipee, ending about 12 km from Wolfeboro, with a spurious anchor vertex at the Sanbornville end that made the line double back on itself. It now follows the branch's own right of way, assembled from the OSM ways tagged 'Wolfeboro Railroad' / 'Wolfeboro Railroad (Cotton Valley Speeder Club)' and the Cotton Valley Trail and Bridge Falls Path that occupy the corridor today, running west from the Conway Branch junction at Sanbornville to the Wolfeboro terminus. Traced length 19.1 km (11.9 miles), consistent with the documented 12-mile branch.

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
